items.t: Radiator leaks coolant into the transmission
items.job: Replace radiator and flush transmission fluid
items.note: Parts: Nissan Value Advantage radiator about $253 (genuine-equivalent, list $375), aftermarket about $277, CSF all-aluminum about $489. Labor from YourMechanic (average $252 labor; its per-year totals run about $1,190–$1,235 for 2005–2014); the upper hours allow for repeated transmission fluid flushes. If coolant has already damaged the transmission, a rebuild or replacement adds several thousand dollars (Infiniti QX56 twin owners report about $3,900–$6,000).

items.t: Engine knock from scuffed cylinder 7
items.job: Replace short block (lower engine)
items.note: Covered under Nissan's bulletin while the powertrain warranty applies. Owners outside warranty have been quoted about $9,200 to over $10,000.

items.t: Cracked exhaust manifolds
items.job: Replace one exhaust manifold and gaskets
items.note: Parts per side: Dorman 674-843/674-844 about $577–$597, genuine Nissan about $1,385–$1,440. Hours are derived from YourMechanic per-year totals for 2005–2015 ($1,977–$2,453 per side) less parts; no published book time was found. Broken studs add time, and replacing both sides roughly doubles the cost. The Infiniti QX56 twin shows RepairPal at about $2,600–$3,250.

items.t: No-start and BCI warnings from failing brake light switch
items.job: Replace stop lamp (brake light) switch
items.note: The switch itself is cheap; most of the cost is diagnosis.

items.t: Rear A/C lines leak under the truck
items.job: Replace rear A/C refrigerant line section and recharge
items.note: RepairPal estimates about $1,750–$1,900 for refrigerant line replacement; a leak test comes first.

items.t: Rear self-leveling suspension sags
items.job: Replace rear air shocks or convert to coil springs and shocks
items.note: Prices are for 2004–2015 trucks. Low end is YourMechanic average air shock parts ($177; rear air shock jobs about $514–$539 total). High end is the Strutmasters coil-spring conversion kit ($599, about 1 hour per wheel). A failed compressor, solenoid or ride height sensor adds cost.

items.t: Power liftgate stops working
items.job: Tighten liftgate motor bolt and replace gas struts
items.note: Low end is struts and a bolt; high end includes a liftgate motor.

items.t: Emergency braking warning with Ethernet codes
items.job: Reprogram radar (distance sensor) control unit
items.note: Normally covered under the new-vehicle warranty.

items.t: Catalytic converters break up and clog
items.job: Replace one front (manifold) catalytic converter and gaskets
items.note: Parts per side: aftermarket direct-fit kit about $416, MagnaFlow 49356 about $950. Hours are derived from RepairPal's total ($1,418–$1,895 for 2005–2015) less parts; no published book time was found. On this engine the front converters are part of the exhaust manifold, so broken studs add time. Fix any misfire or oil burning first or the new converter can fail too.

items.t: ABS, VDC and brake lights from failing brake booster sensor
items.job: Replace brake booster (includes delta stroke sensor) and bleed brakes
items.note: Parts are the Nissan booster 47210-ZC01A (about $718 discounted, $1,015 list). Hours are derived from RepairPal's 2005–2008 total of $1,289–$1,414 less the part; no published book time was found. Remanufactured boosters exist but confirm they include the sensor.

items.t: Front brake rotors warp early
items.job: Replace front brake rotors (and pads)
items.note: Based on YourMechanic, since no parts-plus-labor source was found: average rotor job $381 ($213 parts, $168 labor); front rotor quotes for 2018–2021 are about $632–$637.
